clue.text: Imaginary character among the first Wells wrote about

definitions.text: Imaginary character among the first Wells wrote about

parts.words: Imaginary character among the first Wells wrote about
parts.note: H. G. Wells wrote The First Men in the Moon; one of those first men would be a figure seen in the lunar face

explanation.surface: A fictional figure from among the earliest books H. G. Wells wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first' reads as Wells's early works, but it is the title The First Men in the Moon; the answer is also the face folk imagine on the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure people fancy they see in the lunar surface is an imaginary character, and Wells's lunar explorers were men there.

clue.text: Poet up in arms

definitions.meaning: the Roman epigrammatist Marcus Valerius Martialis, known in English by this name

explanation.surface: A poet who is up in arms about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial wrote Latin epigrams; the adjective also means warlike, as a soldier armed for battle is.

clue.text: Developing a trail, following new lead

indicators.note: following says the pieces a and trail come after the lead letter of new
the lead of the word new is its opening letter, the one at the front

parts.note: a trail left by an animal is its scent

explanation.surface: A hunter developing a trail by following a fresh lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into being, still emerging and growing.

clue.text: Wishful thinking? For the present, no

definitions.text: Wishful thinking? For the present, no

parts.words: Wishful thinking? For the present, no
parts.note: longing that looks to the past rather than wishing for things now

explanation.surface: Is this wishful thinking? Not about the present, anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the present, no' sounds like a refusal, but it says the wistful longing is not about now: it is aimed at bygone times.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental yearning for a past period, a kind of wistful daydreaming about earlier days.

clue.text: Women's accommodation run by male

parts.note: to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: Lodgings for women are managed by a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women's quarters of a Muslim household, the part set aside for wives and concubines.

clue.text: Sailor leaves a fortune

parts.note: maté is a South American tea brewed from dried leaves
one's lot is one's fate or fortune

explanation.surface: A seaman dies and leaves a large sum in his will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb (bequeaths, departs) but is a noun: the leaves that make maté tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British slang, borrowed from French, for a seaman in the navy.

clue.text: Foreign deliveries, a vast quantity

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, so overs are groups of deliveries
a sea of something is a huge amount of it

explanation.surface: Huge numbers of parcels are arriving from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests post, but it is cricket: an over is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversea is an old variant of overseas, describing things from abroad, beyond the sea.

clue.text: Fool steals pouches outside

parts.note: patch is an old word for a jester or clown, after Cardinal Wolsey's fool
to pocket something is to take it dishonestly

explanation.surface: A clown pilfers bags from outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Patch pockets are flat pouches sewn onto the outer face of a garment rather than set inside it.

clue.text: Puts a stop to a right to take holidays

parts.note: rests are breaks from work, short holidays

explanation.surface: Someone halts a person's right to take time off work.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest a process is to halt it or check its progress.

clue.text: Call for retirement

parts.note: a bugle signal ordering troops to withdraw, or a summons to step back from work

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to stop working and retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests giving up a job, but here it is military withdrawal, sounded on the bugle at sunset or when falling back.
explanation.definitionFit: In the army the retreat is a bugle or drum signal for soldiers to fall back or end the day.

clue.text: Unsmart manoeuvre by board open to changes

indicators.note: a manoeuvre moves things into new positions, so the letters of the word before are reshuffled

parts.note: a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A foolish tactic by the board of directors leaves the company liable to upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' rearranges UNSMART into TRANSMU, to which TABLE is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transmutable can be transformed into another form or nature.

clue.text: Somehow making me rich — a wild fancy that!

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unstated route, so they are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the idea of making the speaker rich is a pipe dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges MERICH into CHIMER, and A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fantastic delusion or impossible dream, named after the mythical hybrid monster.

clue.text: English lass I'm crazy for?

indicators.note: crazy says these letters have gone wild and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A man wonders who the English girl he is mad about might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges E, LASS and IM; the whole clue also describes a girl with this name whom the speaker loves.
explanation.definitionFit: Melissa is a woman's name, so it could belong to the girl the speaker adores.

clue.text: A good many fly

parts.note: pi is crossword shorthand for pious, meaning good
a lot means many

explanation.surface: A great number of insects buzz around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect, but it is the verb: to fly an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot is to steer an aircraft, which is what flying one means.

clue.text: Book in volume a saint composed

parts.note: gal is the abbreviation for gallon, a measure of volume

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of the two words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A saint wrote a book in one volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book in' tempts you to look for a container, but 'in' is only a link; 'composed' gives the anagram of A SAINT, ATIANS, after the gallon abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's epistle to the Galatians is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: One whose standing depends on recognition of his deeds

definitions.text: One whose standing depends on recognition of his deeds

parts.words: One whose standing depends on recognition of his deeds
parts.note: deeds read as legal title documents, and standing as owning property where one stands

explanation.surface: A man whose reputation rests on his achievements being acknowledged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deeds' suggests heroic acts, but they are title deeds, the documents proving ownership of property.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor of estates holds his acres by title deeds, and his status comes from that property.

clue.text: Rants about breaking cash limit

indicators.note: breaking says one piece splits the other open and sits within it

parts.note: coin means money, cash

indicators.note: about means round and about, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a spending cap being breached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rants' looks like the definition but is fodder; 'about' scrambles it to NSTRA, and 'breaking' sets that within the money word. 'limit' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to restrict or hold back within bounds.

clue.text: A river, moreover, goes over here

definitions.text: A river, moreover, goes over here

indicators.note: goes over says the run of letters turns over, reading upwards in this down entry

parts.note: again can mean moreover, besides

explanation.surface: A river tumbles over a drop at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes over' reverses A, R and AGAIN to give the answer; the whole clue describes the falls where a river plunges over a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niagara River pours over the famous falls on the Canada and US border.

clue.text: Finished level — have to fix that

parts.note: a game that finished level was tied
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Someone completes a level and has to repair it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished level' reads as a smoothed surface, but it is a drawn game: tied.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie down is to fasten or secure something firmly in place.

clue.text: Chinese outfit that could be nothing short of famous

indicators.note: could be says the letters might form something else once rearranged
short of says something is missing from the letters before they are rearranged

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Chinese costume might be almost renowned.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from FAMOUS and rearrange FAMUS to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A samfu is a simple Chinese suit of jacket and trousers.

clue.text: Summoned for audition and seen

indicators.note: for audition means for hearing, so the word is spoken and sounds like another

parts.note: to be cited is to be summoned to court

explanation.surface: An actor was called to try out and was noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' suggests an actor trying out, but it means hearing: CITED is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Sighted means spotted or observed.

clue.text: Workaday Union set up with European support

indicators.note: support says the next piece holds up the one above it in the column
set up means raised, so in this down entry the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, a British trade union
a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: A trade union was established with backing from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses the miners' union abbreviation to MUN; in a down clue the Scandinavian below it is its 'support'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mundane means ordinary and everyday, dull like daily routine.

clue.text: Brought back from Lisle Manet's works of art

indicators.note: Brought back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Artworks were returned from a Manet collection in Lisle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the letters inside Lisle Manet's; 'Brought back' says they read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamels are decorative objects made of glassy coating fused onto metal, prized as art.

clue.text: Hard-hearted prejudice upset Indian gentleman

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in this down entry the letters read upwards
hearted says a letter goes into the heart, the middle, of the next word

parts.note: bias is prejudice
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A callous bigotry upset a man of rank in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearted' puts H inside BIAS to make BIHAS, and 'upset' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was a respectful title for a man, especially a European, in colonial India.

clue.text: Paper, say, backed full range of fine material

parts.note: a newspaper is an organ, the mouthpiece of a party or group

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: A to Z covers everything, the full range

explanation.surface: A newspaper supported a full range of fine fabrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns AZ into ZA.
explanation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin, stiff, sheer fabric of silk or synthetic fibre.

clue.text: Where marine creature may be seen, leading to Scot's exclamation?

definitions.text: Where marine creature may be seen, leading to Scot's exclamation?

indicators.note: leading to says the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: a seal is a sea mammal
och is a Scots cry of surprise or regret

explanation.surface: A seal surfaces in a Scottish inlet, prompting a cry from a local.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a Scottish arm of the sea where seals bask and a Scot might exclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea loch is a long inlet of the sea in Scotland, where seals often swim.

clue.text: Game to take in some dancing

parts.note: to net is to take in, earn
a ball is an evening of dancing

explanation.surface: A game you can take part in at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport, played chiefly by women, in which goals are scored through a high ring.

clue.text: Eponymous hero providing riotous descriptions

parts.note: a Dickens novel named after its title character, set during the Gordon Riots of 1780

explanation.surface: A title character whose story is full of wild scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riotous' suggests uproarious fun, but the novel depicts the anti-Catholic Gordon Riots in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens titled the book after its simple-minded hero, who is caught up in the riots it describes.
